fact: The Minister of State for Health said the National Digital Health Blueprint implementation has put at least 7.2 million Nigerians on the National Health Information Exchange Platform.

The Minister of State for Health described a National Health Information Exchange Platform with at least 7.2 million Nigerians registered on it, and separately said over 200 hospitals are integrated with Electronic Medical Records systems and mHealth initiatives; as_of is the document's published date, none being given.

The Minister said the ministry will continue scaling up technology-enabled platforms to deliver a National Health Information Exchange System connecting public and private, tertiary, secondary and primary health facilities.

NCDC, the Healthcare Federation of Nigeria and PharmAccess signed a memorandum framing a pilot of automated private-sector IDSR reporting into NCDC's SORMAS surveillance system, to test interoperable approaches; no facilities or start date are given.

fact: The Health Care Providers Association of Nigeria launched HCPAN Connect, a platform meant to let providers, HMOs, regulators, government and patients exchange and aggregate health data in a central repository, to roll out from Lagos to other cities.
The HMCAN chairman said health data in Nigeria is fragmented across systems that do not speak to one another, with no point of connection.

The Federal Ministry of Health and Social Welfare's architecture document says Nigeria lacks health data standards and a functional health information exchange, that no national health information exchange brings health data together, and that health information stays in the system where it is generated; no date is given for the statement, so the document's publication date is used.
